name: Phishing
text: Phishing attempts to obtain initial access through socially engineered messages, commonly using malicious attachments, links, third-party messaging services, or voice lures. Useful log evidence includes suspicious inbound mail followed by file creation, browser activity, or a new process on the recipient endpoint.
log_clues: inbound email with attachment or URL
document or browser followed by unusual child process
new file shortly after message delivery

name: Valid Accounts
text: An adversary may use legitimate local, domain, cloud, or default credentials to access systems and services. Because authentication can look legitimate, stronger evidence comes from unusual logon time, source, host, geography, logon type, privilege use, or unexpected post-login process activity.
log_clues: successful logon from unusual source
service account used interactively
remote login followed by unusual process execution

name: PowerShell
text: PowerShell can be abused to execute commands and scripts, launch processes, perform discovery, download payloads, or run code in memory. Suspicious evidence often combines PowerShell execution with encoded commands, unusual parent processes, network access, downloads, or security-sensitive child activity.
log_clues: powershell or pwsh process
encoded or obfuscated command line
PowerShell followed by network connection or payload execution

name: Windows Command Shell
text: The Windows command shell can be abused to execute commands, scripts, utilities, and binaries. Command-line activity becomes more suspicious when cmd.exe is launched by unusual parents or chains together discovery, credential, persistence, remote-service, or file-transfer utilities.
log_clues: cmd.exe with uncommon parent
chained net, whoami, sc, schtasks, reg, certutil or similar utilities
shell command followed by network or file activity

name: Scheduled Task
text: Windows Task Scheduler may be abused for one-time or recurring execution, persistence, privileged execution, or remote execution. Useful evidence includes task creation or modification through schtasks, PowerShell, WMI, APIs, or Group Policy followed by execution from an unusual path or account.
log_clues: scheduled task creation or modification
schtasks, WMI or PowerShell task creation
new task followed by execution as SYSTEM or from unusual path

name: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
text: Persistence may be established by adding programs to Windows Run or RunOnce registry keys or startup folders so code executes at logon or boot. Stronger evidence combines registry or startup modification with an unusual binary, script path, or subsequent execution.
log_clues: Run or RunOnce registry modification
file created in Startup folder
startup entry pointing to unusual binary or script

name: LSASS Memory
text: Credential theft may target LSASS process memory to recover passwords, hashes, tickets, or other authentication material. Suspicious evidence includes unusual access to lsass.exe, memory dumping, dump-file creation, or credential-dumping tools executed with administrative or SYSTEM privileges.
log_clues: process opens or reads lsass.exe
LSASS dump file creation
credential dumping utility or suspicious privileged process

name: Domain Account Discovery
text: An adversary may enumerate domain users, groups, and privileged accounts to understand available identities and select later targets. Evidence includes net user or net group domain queries, LDAP enumeration, Active Directory PowerShell cmdlets, or unusual directory queries.
log_clues: net user /domain or net group /domain
Get-ADUser or Get-ADGroupMember
unusual LDAP account enumeration

name: System Information Discovery
text: System information discovery gathers operating-system, hardware, version, patch, architecture, or host metadata that can guide later actions. Evidence includes systeminfo, hostname, uname, lscpu, OS-release reads, registry inspection, or equivalent cloud and virtualization queries.
log_clues: systeminfo, hostname, uname or lscpu
OS version or architecture queries
host metadata enumeration shortly after execution

name: Remote System Discovery
text: Remote system discovery identifies other hosts, addresses, names, or network infrastructure that may support lateral movement. Evidence includes rapid ping or ARP activity, net view, directory queries for computers, host-file inspection, or network-device neighbor enumeration.
log_clues: rapid host or IP enumeration
ping, arp, net view, LDAP computer queries
neighbor or routing discovery before lateral movement

name: Remote Desktop Protocol
text: RDP may be used with valid credentials to obtain an interactive session on another Windows system and continue activity as the logged-on user. Stronger evidence combines remote logon with unusual source hosts, new destinations, privilege use, file access, or post-login process execution.
log_clues: RDP or Remote Desktop logon
new source-to-destination host relationship
remote logon followed by unusual process or file activity

name: SMB / Windows Admin Shares
text: SMB and Windows administrative shares such as ADMIN$ or C$ may be used with valid credentials to copy files, access remote resources, and support remote execution. Strong evidence combines authenticated SMB access with file transfer, service creation, scheduled tasks, or execution on the destination host.
log_clues: access to ADMIN$, C$ or IPC$
authenticated SMB file copy
SMB activity followed by remote service or task execution

name: Ingress Tool Transfer
text: An adversary may transfer tools or payloads from an external system into a compromised environment, or move tools between victim systems. Useful evidence correlates an unusual process or shell making a network connection with creation of a new executable, script, archive, or payload file.
log_clues: curl, wget, certutil, PowerShell or similar downloader
external connection followed by file creation
new tool or payload appearing on compromised host

name: Web Protocols
text: HTTP, HTTPS, or WebSocket traffic may be used for command and control because web protocols blend with normal network activity. Suspicious evidence includes uncommon processes communicating with rare domains, repetitive beacon-like traffic, unusual headers, encoded request content, or web traffic on unexpected ports.
log_clues: non-browser process using HTTP or HTTPS
periodic beacon-like connections
rare destination with unusual headers or encoded content

name: Archive via Utility
text: Collected data may be compressed, packaged, or encrypted with utilities such as 7-Zip, WinRAR, zip, tar, makecab, or similar tools before transfer. Evidence is stronger when archive creation occurs in staging or temporary directories after access to many files and before outbound transfer.
log_clues: 7z, rar, zip, tar, makecab or archive utility
large archive created in staging directory
archive creation followed by outbound transfer

name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
text: Stolen data may be exfiltrated over an existing command-and-control channel so outbound transfer resembles normal C2 communication. Evidence includes unusual outbound data volume or file access followed by transmission from a process already associated with suspicious remote communications.
log_clues: outbound transfer over established C2 destination
large or unusual upload after collection
suspicious process reads files then sends network data

name: Data Encrypted for Impact
text: An adversary may encrypt files, storage objects, virtual-machine data, or other resources to disrupt availability, commonly as ransomware or destructive activity. Evidence includes high-rate file rewrites or renames, new extensions, encryption utilities, ransom notes, or attempts to affect many local and remote files.
log_clues: rapid file modification or rename across many files
new encrypted extensions or ransom notes
encryption process touching local, network or VM storage
